newsitem.title: USA: North America bunkers skyrocket, volatile trade.
newsitem.headline: North America bunkers skyrocket, volatile trade.

text.p: North American bunker prices skyrocketed in volatile trade late this week, pulled up by heating oil futures and low stocks of residual fuel, traders said Thursday.
Players said shipowners, many with low tanks, had been waiting for values to lower but quickly dove into the market on fears the rally will continue.
"Heating oil is a big factor in the market but the residual fuel oil is practically non-existent," said one U.S. East Coast trader.
The rally is expected to last into next week.
In New York Harbor, 380 CST soared $15 to between $143/145 a tonne, with 180 CST up to $148/149 after a supplier with $136 sold out.
Houston 380 CST traded between $130/132, and 180 CST between $135/136, $15 above Tuesday levels.
Players are keeping their eye on Singapore to see how it reacts to the price spike and possibly create more wild activity in the U.S. bunker market.

"The big factor is the Far East and how they behave. If they hold down their numbers ships will bunker out there. If they just react, and raise their prices then we will see some volatility out here," said a U.S. trader.
West Coast remained largely quiet, with Los Angeles 380 CST edging up $2 to $119/121.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk + 1 212 859-1631
